caption:
OpenAI is bringing in Cathedral Systems, the startup founded by former DOGE staffers whose AI agents got into some of Anthropic's internal systems last month.
Cathedral's researchers will use OpenAI's own models to attack OpenAI's defenses in its next security sprint.
OpenAI also raised its bug bounty: exceptional finds can now pay about $172,000 with bonuses.

Would you hire the hackers who broke into your biggest rival?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Interesting Engineering, FourWeekMBA · Photos: Wikimedia Commons, Decrypt, CoinCentral

site_article.answer_summary: OpenAI is partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use OpenAI's models to challenge its defenses, and it raised critical bug rewards to up to $30,000, with exceptional findings worth about $172,000 with bonuses.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI is partnering with Cathedral Systems for its next internal security sprint, in which outside researchers will use OpenAI's models alongside its own teams to challenge the company's defenses. OpenAI described the plan in posts dated November 2, 2026, and announced it on X on November 3, according to Interesting Engineering and FourWeekMBA.

OpenAI did not give a start date, duration, fee or scope for the sprint, FourWeekMBA and Data Studios reported. In its previous sprint, about 25 percent of OpenAI's product engineers worked on finding and fixing weaknesses, using Codex to investigate findings, reproduce vulnerabilities in isolated environments and prepare patches, Interesting Engineering reported.

Cathedral is a cybersecurity startup that uses AI. Its chief executive and cofounder is Gavin Kliger, and its founders are former staffers of the Department of Government Efficiency, according to FourWeekMBA, which cited Quartz. The company closed a $160 million round in July at a $1.4 billion valuation, FourWeekMBA reported, citing Decrypt.

In October, Cathedral probed Anthropic through a program modeled on a bug bounty. A draft report described by The Washington Post on October 26 said its agents reached meeting transcripts, salary and job offer details, and Slack messages about Anthropic's advanced models, through flaws in outside vendors' admin and sales tools, FourWeekMBA reported.

Anthropic confirmed access to a limited set of its sales, HR and IT systems and said customer conversations, source code and model weights were not touched. It said its monitoring flagged some of the activity, that it cut off access the same day, and that Cathedral exaggerated the national security implications and did not fully follow the program's rules. Cathedral's draft said data access was kept to a minimum. OpenAI's announcement does not mention the Anthropic episode, Data Studios noted.

Kliger said OpenAI is setting an example by partnering with outside security firms and that every company should be thinking about how to put these capabilities to work, according to Interesting Engineering.

OpenAI also raised its security bug bounty. Critical findings in ChatGPT, Codex or the API Platform can now earn up to $30,000, and the company said the midpoint of its reward ranges for medium, high and critical findings rose more than fourfold on average. Exceptional findings, previously capped at $100,000, keep that base but can now reach about $172,000 with bonuses, according to FourWeekMBA and Data Studios.

The new ranges apply to reports not yet awarded, and researchers paid in the 30 days before the change will receive the difference. Model safety issues and jailbreaks stay in a separate safety program, Data Studios reported. OpenAI also committed $1 billion in subsidized access over six months through Daybreak for defenders who protect essential services and digital infrastructure.

The choice of partner stands out. Cathedral's public profile comes largely from its disputed account of reaching Anthropic's internal systems, and OpenAI is now inviting the same team to test its own defenses with its own models. Together with higher bounties, the move shows OpenAI treating AI assisted attacks as a near term threat that it would rather face from paid researchers first.
OpenAI's security team is due at the PROMPT2PWN event in Oakland on November 20 and 21; any published results from the Cathedral sprint would be the first real test of what this partnership finds.
